newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-LEONARD PUTTS SUPERBLY TO WIN BRITISH OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEONARD PUTTS SUPERBLY TO WIN BRITISH OPEN.

text.p: American Justin Leonard putted supremely for a six-under-par 65 and overhauled Jesper Parnevik of Sweden to capture the British Open golf title by three strokes on Sunday.

The unheralded former U.S. amateur champion rifled in putts from all over the greens of Royal Troon including birdies from 15 feet and 35 feet at the 16th and 17th holes as once again Parnevik was denied the title.

It seemed most likely to go to the Swede for most of the day but Parnevik, who lost the 1994 Open at Turnberry to Nick Price when he bogeyed the final hole, missed a vital four-foot birdie putt at the 16th hole.
Then he bogeyed the last two holes to drop back into a tie for second place with Northern Irishman Darren Clarke.
Leonard, winning only his third title as a professional, finished with a 12-under-par total of 272. Parnevik had a final round two-over-par 73 while Clarke compiled a level-par 71.
"I made the putts I missed yesterday," said Leonard, who shot a one-over-par 72 on Saturday.
"I can't believe how calm I was right up until the 18th green."
